literal: Xie repeatedly spoke in person of the late emperor's intent, asking to fulfill his long-held wish.
idiomatic: Xie spoke again and again at court of the late emperor's intent, begging leave to fulfill the wish he had nursed for years.

literal: The emperor answered Xie in grief and would not grant it each time.
idiomatic: Each time the emperor answered him in tears and would not consent.

literal: He memorialized again and again in earnest; the emperor could not go against the late charge and indulged his refined wish.
idiomatic: Xie tabled memorial after memorial, so earnest that the emperor could not defy his father's charge and at last granted the life Xie had asked for.

literal: Still pressed with an outside appointment, he was made Xie Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Even so they pressed an outside post on him: Xie was made commander-in-chief and governor of Dingzhou.

literal: Xie again memorialized refusal; the emperor would not allow it, and he took up the post.
idiomatic: Xie refused again; the emperor would not hear of it, and he went to his duties.

literal: The emperor wrote Xie a letter of utmost familial respect, asking Xie to enter the capital.
idiomatic: The emperor wrote to him with the deference of kin and begged him to return to the capital.

literal: At the start of Jingming, Qi Governor of Yuzhou Pei Shuye turned Shouyang over to Wei; an edict made Xie commander of southern campaign forces to meet Minister of Works Wang Su in receiving Shouyang.
idiomatic: Early in Jingming, Pei Shuye, Qi governor of Yuzhou, surrendered Shouyang to Wei. Xie was ordered to command the southern armies and join Wang Su, director of the secretariat, in taking the city.

literal: He was again appointed Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was again made minister of works.

literal: An edict also made him, in his existing office, Governor of Yangzhou, promoted to Grand Marshal while retaining Minister of Works.
idiomatic: An edict named him governor of Yangzhou in his existing rank, promoted him to grand marshal, and left him minister of works.

literal: Qi general Chen Bozhi camped at Feikou; Hu Song also held Liangcheng.
idiomatic: The Qi general Chen Bozhi held Feikou; Hu Song held Liangcheng.

literal: Xie disposed his officers and soldiers; in repeated battles he broke them.
idiomatic: Xie arrayed his commanders and broke them battle after battle.

literal: When Huainan was pacified, Xie was summoned back to court.
idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, the court recalled him.

literal: At first, when Xie secured Shouyang, he captured several men including Qi Governor of Ruyin Wang Guo and Attendant of Yuzhou Yu Ji.
idiomatic: When he first took Shouyang he had captured Qi officials among them Wang Guo, governor of Ruyin, and Yu Ji, attendant of Yuzhou.

literal: Xie treated them with open courtesy and often had them at his table.
idiomatic: Xie received them with open courtesy and kept them at his table.

literal: Guo seized an opening to ask return beyond the river; Xie with sympathy granted it.
idiomatic: Guo found a moment to ask leave to return south of the Yangtze; Xie granted it from sympathy.

literal: Guo again thanked him, saying: "We who return now bear your gracious favor on our backs; please allow your benevolent host to shake the army and turn our tracks beyond the river."
idiomatic: Guo thanked him again: "We who go home now carry your grace on our backs. Grant your noble host leave to march and turn our footsteps back across the river."

literal: Only then did they return.
idiomatic: Only then did they depart.

literal: Such was how the distant held him in regard.
idiomatic: So deep was the regard he won from men far away.

literal: When Xie reached the capital he repeatedly memorialized to resign as Grand Marshal and Minister of Works and the added fiefs, begging return to Zhongshan; an edict would not allow it.
idiomatic: Back in the capital, he repeatedly asked to lay down grand marshal, minister of works, and the added fiefs and retire to Zhongshan; the edict refused.

literal: He was made Director of the Secretariat; Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works as before; he firmly refused but could not escape.
idiomatic: They made him director of the secretariat while keeping his other posts; he refused until he could refuse no more.

literal: At the time Prince of Xianyang Xi was arrogant and had many unlawful acts; Prince of Beihai Xiang spoke of it privately to the emperor;
idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Xi had grown proud and lawless; Prince of Beihai Xiang whispered as much to the emperor.

literal: He also said Xie had won great popular favor and ought not long remain at the head of government, urging the emperor to follow the late charge.
idiomatic: He also said Xie had won the people's hearts and should not long head the government, urging the emperor to honor his father's last wish.

literal: Xi and the others also sent out Commander of the Palace Guard Yu Lie as Governor of Hengzhou; Lie was deeply resentful.
idiomatic: Xi and his party also posted Commander of the Palace Guard Yu Lie to Hengzhou, and Lie burned with resentment.

literal: Lie's son Zhong was constantly at the emperor's side; he secretly had Zhong speak to the emperor that he ought early to take government into his own hands.
idiomatic: Lie's son Zhong was always at the emperor's ear; Lie secretly had him urge the young ruler to take the reins himself.

literal: When the time came for the suburban sacrifice, princes and nobles all fasted in the east wing of the temple.
idiomatic: When the season came for the suburban sacrifice, princes and nobles fasted together in the temple's east wing.

literal: The emperor sent Yu Lie with sixty stalwart guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to audience.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Yu Lie with sixty picked guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to audience.

literal: The emperor said to Xie: "Of late north and south affairs have been pressing; I could not honor your lofty withdrawal.
idiomatic: He told Xie, "North and south have both been on fire; I could not grant the lofty retreat you sought.

literal: What sort of man is Ke that he dared long defy the former charge?
idiomatic: What is Ke, that he dared so long to defy my father's command?

literal: Now I grant my uncle's wish to walk apart from power."
idiomatic: Now I grant my uncle the high road he has long desired."

literal: An edict then built a residence for Xie, kept deliberately plain, to satisfy his heart.
idiomatic: An edict built him a house deliberately plain, to satisfy his heart.

literal: Xie thereupon wrote "Rhapsody on the Fly" to voice his feelings.
idiomatic: Xie answered with a "Rhapsody on the Fly" to voice what he felt.

literal: He was again made Grand Preceptor; Xie firmly refused.
idiomatic: They named him grand preceptor; he refused again.

literal: An edict had the attendant-in-ordinary urge him earnestly; the emperor again wrote Xie a letter of familial respect; Xie could not refuse and accepted.
idiomatic: The attendant-in-ordinary was sent to press him; the emperor wrote again with familial deference; at last Xie yielded.

literal: Before and after, the emperor repeatedly visited Xie's residence.
idiomatic: Again and again the emperor came to his gate.

literal: When the princes of Jingzhao and Guangping were violent and lawless, an order had squad leaders of the palace guard lead armored guards to confine the princes in their residences; Xie memorialized in sharp remonstrance; the emperor did not accept it.
idiomatic: When the princes of Jingzhao and Guangping turned brutal and lawless, the throne ordered squad leaders of the guard to pen them in their houses with armored men. Xie remonstrated in the sharpest terms; the emperor would not listen.

literal: At the time they were deliberating law codes; Xie with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, the eight ministers, and court scholars of talent met every five days to discuss whether the statutes should stand or fall.
idiomatic: While the realm debated new law codes, Xie met every five days with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, the eight ministers, and the ablest scholars to weigh what should stand or fall.

literal: Whatever they decided, men of the age looked up to them.
idiomatic: Whatever they decided, the age looked up to them.

literal: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: Xie honored letters and history; he compiled from ancient emperors and worthies down to Wei imperial sons and clansmen thirty scrolls titled Essentials in Brief.
idiomatic: Xie loved letters and history and compiled thirty scrolls, from ancient emperors and sages down to Wei princes and kin, titled Essentials in Brief.

literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial.
idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and filial.

literal: Speaking at court, he had his maternal uncle Pan Senggu made Governor of Changle.
idiomatic: At court he secured his maternal uncle Pan Senggu the governorship of Changle.

literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu plotted rebellion, Senggu was forced along.
idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rose in rebellion, Senggu was dragged into it.

literal: Director of the Secretariat Gao Zhao was by nature fierce and obstinate; moreover Zhao's elder brother's daughter had entered as consort.
idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Gao Zhao was fierce and obstinate by nature, and his elder brother's daughter had lately entered the inner quarters.

literal: When Empress Shun died the emperor wished to make her empress; Xie firmly held it impossible.
idiomatic: When Empress Shun died the emperor wished to raise her to empress; Xie held the move impossible and would not yield.

literal: Zhao then slandered Xie again and again; through Senggu's tie to Yu's rebellion Zhao accused Xie of communicating with Yu and summoning southern barbarians.
idiomatic: Zhao slandered him without cease, and through Senggu's link to Yu's plot accused Xie of conspiring with Yu and calling southern rebels.

literal: Xie's Bureau Director Wei Yan and former gate officer Gao Zuzhen hoped for Zhao's patronage and fabricated the affair.
idiomatic: Xie's bureau director Wei Yan and former gate officer Gao Zuzhen, hungry for Zhao's favor, fabricated the case.

literal: At first Zhao had Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui present the memorial; Hui would not.
idiomatic: Zhao first ordered Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Hui to present the accusation; Hui refused.

literal: He then had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak of it.
idiomatic: He then had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak of it.

literal: The emperor questioned Hui; Hui made clear Xie had done none of this.
idiomatic: The emperor questioned Hui, who made clear that Xie had done none of this.

literal: The emperor questioned Zhao again; Zhao took Wei Yan and Zuzhen as proof, and then believed it.
idiomatic: The emperor questioned Zhao again; Zhao produced Wei Yan and Zuzhen as witnesses, and the emperor believed him.

literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Yongping, Xie was summoned with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Prince of Guangyang Jia, Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Guangping Huai, and Gao Zhao and others.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongping 1, Xie was summoned with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Prince of Guangyang Jia, Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Guangping Huai, Gao Zhao, and others.

literal: At the time Xie's consort was in childbirth; he firmly refused but could not; his mind was full of dread; he took leave of his consort and mounted the carriage.
idiomatic: His consort was in labor; he tried to refuse and could not, sick with dread. He took leave of her and climbed into the carriage.

literal: Entering the east side gate, crossing a small bridge, the ox was hurt; men pulled and entered.
idiomatic: At the east side gate, crossing a little bridge, the ox was injured; men hauled the carriage through.

literal: They feasted in the forbidden precinct; at night all were drunk; each went to a separate place to rest.
idiomatic: They feasted inside the palace until all were drunk, then each went to a separate room to sleep.

literal: Soon Yuan Zhen came with guards bearing poisoned wine.
idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zhen came with guards bearing poisoned wine.

literal: Xie said: "Once I see the August One, I die without regret."
idiomatic: Xie said, "Let me see the Son of Heaven once more and I die without regret."

literal: Zhen said: "How can the August One be seen again!"
idiomatic: Zhen said, "The Son of Heaven will not be seen again."

literal: Guards struck Xie twice with the ring of the blade; Xie cried out that he was wronged.
idiomatic: Guards struck him twice with the flat of the blade; Xie cried that he was wronged.

literal: Guards again struck Xie with the blade; then he drank the poison; guards then killed him.
idiomatic: They struck him again, then he drank; the guards finished him.

literal: Toward dawn the corpse was wrapped in a quilt, carried out through the screen gate, and the body returned to his residence; it was said he had died from drink.
idiomatic: Toward dawn they wrapped the corpse in quilts, carried it out through the screen gate, and sent it home, saying he had died from drink.

literal: Xie's consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed: "Gao Zhao killed a man by perverting justice; Heaven has a spirit—you will yet die a vile death."
idiomatic: His consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed, "Gao Zhao murdered him by twisting the law. Heaven has eyes—you will yet die foully."

literal: When Zhao was executed for crime he returned to this very house; commentators knew there was retribution.
idiomatic: When Zhao was executed for his crimes he was brought back to this very house; men said Heaven had answered her.

literal: The emperor held mourning for him in the eastern hall.
idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in the eastern hall.

literal: Xie had great merit for the state yet was killed without crime; men and women on the road all wept and said: "Gao Zhao, that petty man, wrongly killed so worthy a prince!"
idiomatic: Xie had served the state with great merit and died innocent; men and women in the streets wept and said, "That petty man Gao Zhao murdered a prince so worthy as this!"

literal: Nobles at court all lost heart.
idiomatic: The great at court lost heart.

literal: At Jingming and Baode monasteries the monks were about to ring for the meal when they suddenly heard of Xie's death; more than a thousand in the two monasteries all sighed in pain, would not eat, and drank only water in fast.
idiomatic: At the Jingming and Baode monasteries the monks were ringing for the midday meal when word came of Xie's death; more than a thousand monks in both houses groaned, would not eat, and drank only water in mourning.

literal: Posthumously he was given the golden axe, commissioner with credentials, commander of all armies within and without, Minister of Works, Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: Posthumously they gave him the golden axe, credentials as commissioner, command of all armies at home and abroad, minister of works, and grand preceptor.

literal: He was given the imperial canopy with nine tassels, a hundred guards with halberds and swords, feathered banners and drums before and behind, and the imperial carriage.
idiomatic: They granted the imperial canopy with nine tassels, a hundred guards with halberds and swords, feathered banners and drums before and behind, and the imperial carriage.

literal: The relevant office memorialized Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Liu Fang's discussion of Xie's posthumous name: preserving greatness and fixing merit is Wu, good inquiry and thorough penetration is Xuan; the posthumous name should be Prince Wu Xuan.
idiomatic: The ministry reported Director Liu Fang's judgment on his posthumous name: "Preserving greatness and fixing merit" yields Wu; "good inquiry and thorough penetration" yields Xuan. He should be Prince Wu Xuan.

literal: The edict approved.
idiomatic: The edict approved.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wen Mu; his consort Lady Li was Empress Wen Mu; the spirit tablet was moved to the ancestral temple and called Ancestor Su.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne he was posthumously titled Emperor Wen Mu and Lady Li Empress Wen Mu; his tablet entered the ancestral temple as Ancestor Su.

literal: Under Emperor Jiemin his spirit tablet was removed.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin his spirit tablet was removed.

literal: His eldest son Shao, styled Zinuo, succeeded to the fief.
idiomatic: His eldest son Shao, styled Zinuo, succeeded to the fief.

literal: Shao was skilled in martial arts and in youth had spirit.
idiomatic: Shao was skilled in arms and in youth had mettle.

literal: Early in Mingdi, when Liang generals raided the border, Shao memorialized nine thousand dan of grain, six hundred bolts of silk and goods, and two hundred household officials of the fief to supply the army.
idiomatic: Early in Mingdi, when Liang generals raided the border, Shao offered nine thousand dan of grain, six hundred bolts of silk and goods, and two hundred household officials of the fief for the army.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling praised his utmost intent and would not accept it.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling praised his devotion and would not accept it.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: He rose step by step to governor of Qingzhou.

literal: Late in Xiaochang, when Empress Dowager Ling lost virtue and the four quarters were in turmoil, Shao then harbored a different intent.
idiomatic: Late in Xiaochang, when the empress dowager lost her virtue and the realm boiled, Shao nursed designs of his own.

literal: Prince of Anfeng Yanming reported him; he was summoned in as Imperial Censor.
idiomatic: Prince of Anfeng Yanming denounced him; he was summoned in as imperial censor.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, Shao was honored as Prince Without Superior.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Shao was honored as Prince Without Superior.

literal: Soon he met disaster at Heyin.
idiomatic: Soon he met disaster at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Xiao Xuan; his wife Lady Li was Empress Wen Gong.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Xiao Xuan; his wife Lady Li was Empress Wen Gong.

literal: His son Shao, styled Shizhou, loved learning and had a handsome bearing.
idiomatic: His son Shao, styled Shizhou, loved learning and was handsome of bearing.

literal: At first, when Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, his father Shao in fear placed Shao with his trusted friend Governor of Rongyang Zheng Zhongming.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, his father Shao in fear placed the boy with his trusted friend Zheng Zhongming, governor of Rongyang.

literal: Soon Zhongming was killed by men of the city.
idiomatic: Soon Zhongming was killed by men of the city.

literal: Shao in the turmoil lost his wet nurse and with Zhongming's nephew Sengfu fled for refuge.
idiomatic: In the turmoil Shao lost his wet nurse and fled with Zhongming's nephew Sengfu.

literal: On the road they were pressed by bandits; Sengfu feared they could not escape and had Shao dismount.
idiomatic: On the road bandits closed in; Sengfu feared they could not escape and made Shao dismount.

literal: Sengfu said to the travelers: "A bird at the end of flight still finds pity when it casts itself on man—how can you abandon a prince of the blood?"
idiomatic: Sengfu told the travelers, "A bird at the end of its flight still wins pity when it casts itself on a man—how can you abandon a prince of the blood?"

literal: Sengfu raised the blade to press them; the travelers then withdrew.
idiomatic: Sengfu raised his blade and pressed them; they withdrew.

literal: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng who pitied him and hid him in a private house.
idiomatic: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng who pitied him and hid him in her house.

literal: After more than ten days Emperor Zhuang found him by inquiry; he succeeded to Prince of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: After more than ten days Emperor Zhuang found him by inquiry; he succeeded as Prince of Pengcheng.

literal: After Qi Shenwu made Emperor Xiaowu's consort his wife, many of Wei's rare treasures followed her into Shao's house.
idiomatic: After Qi Shenwu gave him Emperor Xiaowu's consort as wife, many of Wei's rare treasures followed her into Shao's house.

literal: There were two jade bowls nested so they could turn but not be separated.
idiomatic: There were two nested jade bowls that could turn but never be pulled apart.

literal: An agate case held three sheng, seamed in jade.
idiomatic: An agate case held three sheng, its seams traced in jade.

literal: All were said to be the work of Western Region demons.
idiomatic: Men said they were the work of demons from the Western Regions.

literal: He held posts as Grand Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Governor of Sizhou, Special Grandee, and Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: He served as grand commandant, attendant-in-ordinary, director of the secretariat, governor of Sizhou, special grandee, and grand tutor.

literal: In the tenth year the imperial astronomers memorialized: "This year the old should be removed and the new spread."
idiomatic: In the tenth year the astronomers reported, "This year the old must be swept away and the new spread."

literal: Emperor Wen Xuan said to Shao: "Why did Han Guangwu revive the dynasty?"
idiomatic: Emperor Wen Xuan asked Shao, "Why did Han's Guangwu restore the dynasty?"

literal: Shao said: "Because he did not kill all the Liu to the last man."
idiomatic: Shao said, "Because he did not kill every Liu to the last man."

literal: Thereupon he killed the various Yuan to appease it.
idiomatic: Thereupon he killed the Yuan to appease the omen.
